svg.title: Flower Anatomy Drag and Drop
svg.desc: A static, simulated drag-and-drop learning activity labeling the parts of a flower.
svg.text: LABEL THE DIAGRAM · FLOWER, SIDE VIEW

g.text: Read each label in the word bank below.
Drag a tile onto the numbered slot that
matches the flower part the arrow points to.
Stuck? Press Hint. Finished? Press Check
Answer to compare with the answer key.
Press Reset to clear the board and retry.

svg.text: Guided mode: click any tile in the word bank to see
it snap into its correct slot automatically.

g.text: Pollination is the transfer of pollen grains from the
anther (male part) to the stigma (female part). Bees,
birds and wind move pollen between flowers, allowing
fertilization — the first step toward seeds and fruit.

svg.text: WORD BANK · DRAG A LABEL TILE INTO ITS NUMBERED SLOT
Static SVG learning demo · no JavaScript · links use #anchor targets

g.text: The pistil is the female part, made of three sections:
sticky stigma on top, tube-like style, ovary at the base.
The stamen is the male part: a slender filament holds
up the anther, which produces yellow pollen grains.
Sepals are the small green leaves just under the petals —
they protected the flower while it was still a bud.
The receptacle is the thickened tip of the stem where
every part of the flower attaches.
Remember: petals attract pollinators; sepals protect the bud.
Compare your board with the correct placements:
Well done! Press Reset and try again without help.
All tiles are back in the word bank.
Place each label into its numbered slot to begin again.
